name: shader
description: The OPTIONAL shader runtime of the effects layer (ADR 0022): aurora (the brand colour moving through a fill or a ground) and halo (light travelling round a surface that works or listens). startShaders() — server-safe, reference-counted, returns its stop function — finds every .fx-aurora / .fx-halo root, mounts one canvas in the part the effect paints and draws it from tokens read where that part sits, through ONE shared WebGL2 context. A shader is admitted only if it paints pixels it owns, takes every input from a token, keeps the component as its floor and guards the contrast of the ink on its part per pixel; check:fx enforces the first two on the sources. The canvas draws the part's own rounded shape (iOS Safari drops a CSS clip on an animating canvas), covers the border box, sits under the part's content or directly after a track's fill so a Slider's thumb stays on top, and follows the component's own state transitions through registered properties (--ui-fx-on, --ui-fx-halo-strength). State is published on the root as data-fx-aurora / data-fx-halo (live, still, floor, lost, unsupported); reduced motion draws one chosen still frame and the loop sleeps when nothing moves. configureShaders() and sampleShader() exist for stories and contrast tests.
